standard_prerequisites: Context span 2249-2261: A = k[z_1, z_2, ...]/(all pairwise products z_i z_j, i != j), S = Spec(A), s the closed point of the maximal ideal (z_i); S - {s} = union of the D(z_i), each D(z_i) open irreducible with generic point eta_i; any quasi-compact open V of S - {s} dense in S - {s} would contain all eta_i, but a principal affine open D(f) with f in (z_1, z_2, ...) lies in (z_1, ..., z_n) for some n and contains only finitely many eta_i, so V cannot be quasi-compact

Context span 2263-2274: B = k[x, z_1, z_2, ...]/(x z_i for all i and all pairwise products z_i z_j), T = Spec(B), U = D(x); for t the closed point of (x, z_i) the closure of U is U cup {t}; a quasi-compact open V with V cap U = empty and U cup V dense in T would be a quasi-compact open of union_i D(z_i) dense in union_i D(z_i), which the first paragraph excludes
core_obligations: Item 2: S with closed point s: by the context, S - {s} contains no quasi-compact open dense in S - {s}
Item 1: T with affine open U = D(x): by the context closure computation and the first paragraph, there is no quasi-compact open V with V cap U = empty and U cup V dense in T
Both S and T are affine schemes, proving the two items of the lemma
proof_roadmap: Read the no-quasi-compact-dense-open claim for S - {s} off the first context paragraph
Transfer it to the complement of U = D(x) in T via the closure computation in the second paragraph
